newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares greet new year with sharp climb.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares greet new year with sharp climb.

text.p: Greek shares greeted the new year with a bang with the benchmark share index gaining 2.26 percent to settle at 954.54 points on volume of 6.63 billion drachmas and brokers in a more upbeat mood.
Bank shares led the advance with the respective index jumping 3.08 percent as shares of National Bank gained 3.95 percent to chase Alpha Credit Bank which climbed a swift 4.7 percent.

"The market started the new year with a strong showing as banks lead the advance. Retail investors still show moderate interest in equities but we will very likely witness a reallocation of funds into stocks this year," said a floor trader.
Other sectors fared well on Thursday including small-caps, up 2.09 percent, construction and industrials which rose 1.04 and 1.44 percent respectively.

"The poor market sentiment in 1996 is reversing and the outlook this year is positive. We anticipate a further decline in inflation and interest rates this year. Also the new 7.5 percent tax on state debt securities will enhance listed companies' dividend yields," said Kappa Securities in its weekly outlook.
Gainers led decliners 152 to 54 with 26 shares unchanged on 232 traded. Turnover was 6.63 billion drachmas on volume of 3.0 million shares, boosted by active block trading.
